problem_type: A paid generation request can leave Nomi for a shot that has no node on the canvas
symptom: Production runs (agent paid card, external MCP, batch continue / recovery) dispatched shots whose canvas landing had failed or never happened: multi-shot landing was best-effort and failures still dispatched, single-shot submitted first and landed afterwards, the in-process stdio MCP never landed, and a result arriving for a deleted node was silently dropped.
direct_cause: appIntegration start called landCanvasBestEffort (swallowing failures) before kicking the scheduler and after submission.start for single shots; the batch scheduler and submission.start never looked at the shot's node binding; attachShotResult returned node-removed without holding the outcome.
class_root: The paid dispatch boundary (submission.start) only checked Run-ledger facts (claim, authorization, consent) and never required that the shot is bound to a landed canvas node, so canvas landing was an optional side path every new dispatch caller could skip.
affected_population: Agent panel paid-card confirmations (single and multi-shot)
External MCP nomi_start_generation through the GUI or the in-process stdio entry
Document-sourced plans confirmed before being placed on the canvas
entry_points: Batch scheduler drives: start / continue / rework / restart recovery
Production result backfill for a deleted node (materializeShots follow / attachShotResult)

external_sources.purpose: Branded (nominal-ish) types so only the admission function can construct the token submission.start requires.

invariants: submission.start only accepts a LandedShotAdmission and re-verifies it against the durable Run before the first durable write and again under the Run lock.
A shot that could not land is never dispatched; the Run rests at needs_attention with stop reason landing_failed, which a retry lifts.
A production outcome arriving while its bound node is absent is held by nodeId and lands when undo / restore brings the node back.

door_reduction.why_not: Dispatch callers of submission.start shrank from four files (appIntegration, mcpStdioServer, scheduler, canvas shot) to three (scheduler, singleShotProductionStart, canvas shot), all forced through one admission by type; the best-effort pre-landing doors in appIntegration are gone. The remaining doors each have one job: five admission callers are distinct user moments that must land before acting (scheduler drive incl. recovery, single-shot start for GUI and stdio, canvas node runs, the paid card before approving, the multi-shot start reporting to the agent); the submission exit re-checks the admission; recordLandingFailure is the single writer of landing_failed; landCanvasForRunOrThrow / landBeforeDispatch / createLandingProjectAccess are the one landing path and its project access; holdOnce is the renderer hold for deleted nodes.

generality_proof: Every paid production dispatch converges on submission.start, whose input type requires a LandedShotAdmission that only admitShotsForDispatch constructs, and whose runtime re-verifies node binding against the durable Run independent of the injectable beforeDispatch hook. A new caller cannot compile without the admission and cannot forge one past the runtime check; the generation-entrances gate additionally requires every entrance to declare node-first or a ledgered exception.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Land unbound shots once, issue admissions only for bound shots, report the rest.
Re-verify an admission against the durable Run inside the submission exit.
Single writer of the landing_failed stop.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: admitForDispatch runs before anchors and shots are dispatched; landFirstMultiShot.test.ts.
Shared by appIntegration and mcpStdioServer; landFirstSingleShot.test.ts and landFirstProjectAccess.test.ts.
Admission before decideGenerationSpend; agentPanelSpendConfirm.e2e.test.ts landing-failure retry case.
origin.nodeId recorded at creation and admitted before sealing.
Approved exception (configuration-time try, no project); reason in scripts/generation-entrances-ledger.json landingExceptions.

recurrence.reason: Every new start moment (ACP agents, new MCP tools, recovery paths) reaches submission.start; without a structural requirement each would have to remember to land first.
same_class_scan: git grep submission.start( in electron non-test: appIntegration, mcpStdioServer, multiShotBatchScheduler, appIntegrationCanvasShot before; scheduler, singleShotProductionStart, appIntegrationCanvasShot after
git grep landCanvasBestEffort: two appIntegration start paths before; zero after
R-gen-doors report (coordinator handoff) plus stdio and paid-card entries found in this line

prevention.invariant: submission.start requires a LandedShotAdmission and re-verifies it against the durable Run.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing admission fails typecheck; a forged or stale admission throws shot_not_landed before any durable write or provider call.
prevention.strategy: Make landing a precondition of the only paid exit, owned by one admission module that also owns the landing_failed state.

legacy_paths.rationale: landCanvasBestEffort (best-effort pre-landing that dispatched anyway) is deleted from the host and both appIntegration start paths in the same change.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is Nomi's own canvas/Run domain rule; no third-party runtime controls it.

invariant_owner_layer.rationale: shotLandingAdmission owns the admission token, its durable re-check (called from the submission exit) and the landing_failed stop; the four test files cover forged tokens, multi/single landing failure and retry, project-not-open handling and the structural callers.

migration: No data migration. Runs already dispatched are unaffected (the check sits before a new dispatch). Canvas consent drafts created by an older build lack origin.nodeId: they are not dispatched, the consent is withdrawn, and the canvas is told canvas_consent_predates_upgrade ("this batch was not sent after the update, confirm again"). Document-plan shots already placed from a storyboard row are adopted by shot identity instead of landing a second node.
residual_risks: Real Electron paid run (multi 2 + single 1 + forced landing failure + MCP cold start hidden window) is unverified in this line; the coordinator runs it.
Writing nodes into a project that is not open (option B) is out of scope; those starts are refused.
Storyboard-placed nodes are adopted only when the shot id is a stable id (storyboardSubjectIdentity STABLE_ID); otherwise the confirm-time landing creates a node, as before.
